provenance_boundary.consequence: This is an exploratory external challenge to a Palmer-generated temporal-shape hypothesis, not a pristine independent preregistration.

biological_hypothesis: Performance-linked colony redistribution is concentrated in a short 2-3 year adult demographic-memory window rather than a 4-5 year natal-recruitment window.

external_biological_anchor.rationale: Adelie recruitment into the breeding population begins around age 3 and is concentrated around ages 4-5 in long-term known-age studies; 4-5 year lags are therefore the biologically expected window for a natal-cohort recruitment echo.
external_biological_anchor.role: Fixes the lag-window interpretation before Signy lag4-lag5 are computed.

analysis.estimator: Reuse exactly the frozen Signy performance-redistribution construction, covariates, colony fixed effects, eligibility and within-season permutation scheme from SIGNY_WIN_STAY_LOSE_SWITCH_REPLICATION_V1.
analysis.inference: Use synchronized within-predictor-season permutations across lag 2-5 models so each permutation yields one C_adult.

decision_language.supported: Signy independently shows the same qualitative short-window-over-recruitment-window temporal shape, strengthening a short-lived demographic-memory interpretation while not establishing individual movement or cue use.
decision_language.unsupported: Do not generalize the Palmer 2-3 year temporal shape beyond Palmer; retain it as a local fixed-specification pattern.

terminal_rules: Do not alter lag windows after observing beta_4 or beta_5.
Do not replace the primary Signy dataset with a favorable sensitivity.
Do not call this a confirmatory independent replication because Signy beta_2 and beta_3 were known before freezing this contract.
Do not infer individual breeding dispersal, prospecting, public-information use or causal cue use from colony-level data.
Do not reinterpret a 4-5 year effect as adult memory if the frozen contrast fails.
